chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
O Umar, do not place a burden upon our Shias, and be kind to them, for the people cannot bear what you can bear.
ai.seo_question: Why should jurists be lenient with the general Shia community?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to the jurist Umar ibn Hanzala, establishes a foundational principle of *taysir* (facilitation) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the rigorous demands placed on scholars and the practical capacity of the general populace. It underscores the scholarly duty of empathy and leniency (*urf*) to prevent religious burden from becoming an obstacle to faith, ensuring that strict adherence remains accessible rather than alienating to the community.
